draft.title: Comparing data sets
card: Compare two data sets on the same scale. You can use a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot, a parallel dot plot or two histograms.
Compare centre first: find the median or mean of each set. Then compare spread: range \(=\) highest value \(-\) lowest value.
Shape
Then compare shape, such as where the data bunches or whether it tails off to one side. Look for outliers, which are values far from the rest.
Meaning
Say what a difference means in context. Example: 9A's range is 6 and 9B's range is 15. So 9B's scores are less consistent than 9A's, because they are more spread out.
draft.remember: Compare two sets on the same scale: centre, spread, shape and outliers.

a.q: Set P is 3, 5, 6, 8, 13. Set Q is 4, 6, 7, 9, 10. Which set has the greater range, and what is it?
opts: P, with a range of 10
Q, with a range of 6
P, with a range of 13
Q, with a range of 10
a.why: The range of P is \(13 - 3 = 10\). The range of Q is \(10 - 4 = 6\). Q's highest value is 10, but its range is found by subtracting, so 10 alone is not its range.
a.clue: Subtract the lowest value from the highest for each set.

b.q: Quiz scores for two Year 9 classes in Melbourne are compared. Class 9A has a median of 14 and a range of 6. Class 9B has a median of 14 and a range of 15. Which statement is correct?
opts: The centres match, but 9B's scores are less consistent
9B has the higher centre and is less consistent
The centres match, and the consistency is the same
9A has the higher centre and is less consistent
b.why: Both medians are 14, so the centres are the same. The range of 9B is 15 and the range of 9A is 6. A larger range means 9B's scores are more spread out, so they are less consistent.
b.clue: Compare the medians, then the ranges, then say what it means.

b.best: The centres match, but 9B's scores are less consistent

problems.detail: Question b reuses the card's worked example almost exactly: classes 9A and 9B, ranges 6 and 15, and the 'less consistent' conclusion. Students can match it from memory rather than apply the idea. Change the numbers or the context.

proposal.title: Comparing two distributions
card: Compare two data sets on the same scale. You can use a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot, a parallel dot plot or two histograms.
Compare centre first: find the median or mean of each set. Then compare spread: range \(=\) highest value \(-\) lowest value.
Then compare shape, such as where the data bunches or whether it tails off to one side. Look for outliers, which are values far from the rest.
Say what each difference means in context. Example: 9A's range is 6 and 9B's range is 15. So 9B's scores are less consistent than 9A's, because they are more spread out.
proposal.remember: Compare centre, spread and shape, then say what each difference means.

a.q: Set P is 3, 5, 6, 8, 13. Set Q is 4, 6, 7, 9, 10. Which set has the greater range, and what is it?
opts: P, with a range of 10
Q, with a range of 6
P, with a range of 13
Q, with a range of 10
a.why: The range of P is \(13 - 3 = 10\). The range of Q is \(10 - 4 = 6\), so P has the greater range. Q's highest value is 10, but a range is found by subtracting, so 10 alone is not its range.
a.clue: Subtract the lowest value from the highest for each set.

b.q: Over a netball season in Bendigo, Ava's goals per game have a median of 12 and a range of 4. Zoe's have a median of 15 and a range of 11. Which statement is correct?
opts: Zoe has the higher centre but is less consistent
Zoe has the higher centre and is more consistent
Ava has the higher centre and is less consistent
Ava has the higher centre and is more consistent
b.why: Zoe's median of 15 is higher than Ava's 12, so Zoe usually scores more. Zoe's range of 11 is larger than Ava's 4, so her scores are more spread out and less consistent. A larger range does not mean more consistent: it means the opposite.
b.clue: Compare the medians first, then think about what a larger range means.
